strategy.summary: Elasto-Dicht Hermannsdorfer is a sound, family-owned seal maker with an engaged owner. It is our single source for the drinking-water O-ring set part:340020, where it owns the tooling. On lip seal part:340040 it holds half the volume and is the cheapest and best-performing source. It is qualified but unused on the aramid gasket part:340030, where its benchmark quote undercut the incumbent. We are a small account to it, and its sales director said it is reviewing small accounts and focusing on customers with volume. The kit bundle (one supplier for all three parts) is therefore our strongest lever. Cost drivers (rubber PPI, labour) justify only a modest rise, and much of that was already absorbed at the last renewal. It historically settles well below its ask. There is little price room, and squeezing hard risks being deprioritised on a single-source part. The evidence is thin: there is no should-cost and only two conversation notes.

persona.style: Moderate, cost-based and open to calculation talks. It asks modestly and settles well below its ask. It is selective about small customers.

It is already the cheapest source on the lip seal and the gasket, so rival data supports its prices. Historically it settles near half its ask or at zero. Realistic room comes from bundle volume (especially moving the gasket to it below the incumbent's price), not from squeezing unit price.

findings.text: No should-cost exists for any of the three parts, so we cannot say how far its prices sit above full cost. The evidence is thin. The owner offered to walk us through his calculation (hourly rates and material), which is the best route to a cost view.

Cost drivers justify roughly +2.5% at most on every part. On 340020: PPI-C2219 +3.9% at weight 0.54 gives +2.11%, and LCI-C +2.7% at weight 0.14 gives +0.37%, about +2.5% in total. On 340040 the total is about +2.4% (+2.11% and +0.32%). On 340030 it is about +2.5% (+2.19% and +0.29%). Both indices are at their 36-month peak, so they argue against a cut, but the weighted rise is modest. Copper, electronics and steel news does not apply to rubber seals.

The 2026 increases (+2.4% on 340020, +2.6% on 340040) already absorbed most of the 12-month driver rise. The indices to 2025-08 were largely priced in at the January 2026 renewal. A further increase now should be well under 2.5%. Under the price clause, prices are fixed per calendar year and changes need 90 days' written notice before year end.

On price, it is the cheapest source we have. On 340040 it sits at 100.98 against Kohlering's 111.69 (rival 10.6% dearer). On 340030 it quoted 1.97 against Ravensteiner's 2.35 but lost the award, and we now pay Ravensteiner 2.23. Rival records therefore support its prices rather than contradict them. Citing them would hurt us.

Room on price is small. In past renewals it settled about 1.7–2.3 pp below its ask, with a final average of about +0.8–0.9%. A realistic settlement on a new ask is about 0 to +1.5%. The larger lever is the kit bundle: moving 340030 to it at about 1.97 would save about 12% on that part. More volume on the other parts also helps, given that it is reviewing small accounts.

findings.text: Family-owned, 45-staff GmbH (turnover EUR 22.9 M, equity 38.9%, credit index 167 stable, VDA 6.3 A). Financially sound with no stress signal, so it can afford to walk away. The owner is personally reachable and engaged in pricing.

The owner offered to walk us through their calculation (hourly rates and material). This is an opening for open-book, cost-based talks. It also lets us test their claimed cost shares against PPI-C2219 (+3.9%) and LCI (+2.7%) instead of accepting asserted drivers.

The sales director said they are reviewing small accounts and will focus on customers with volume. Our spend is about 0.2% of their turnover (EUR 46k). This is a red flag for deprioritisation. Conversely, it means volume is what they need: the 25,000-kit bundle (3 parts, rising forecasts) speaks directly to it.

Contact change: day-to-day sales has moved to a new inside-sales colleague. Decisions likely sit with the sales director and the owner, so escalate bundle and price talks to them rather than to inside sales.

Our payment record is mixed. We are 84.5% late, but only by 2.2 days on average (max 9) on net 30, with no discount abuse. We are broadly reliable but not spotless. Faster or punctual payment is a cheap give, since the contract is already 30 days against our 60-day standard.

Their pricing behaviour is moderate. Prices were flat 2023-2025, rose about 2.5% in 2026, and settled well below their asks. The contract fixes prices per calendar year with 90 days' notice, i.e. by about early October for 2027.
Evidence is thin. There is no news and no letters about cost pressure or capacity, and we have only two short conversation notes.

findings.text: Framework agreement covers part:340020 and part:340040 only. Prices are fixed per calendar year, and any change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end (by about 2 Oct). Payment is 30 days net, against our standard of 60. Delivery is DAP with a 7-day lead time. The quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per supplier-caused complaint. The term runs to 2027-06-30 and auto-extends by 12 months; notice to stop the renewal is due by 2027-04-01.

The supplier settles far below its asks. For 2024 and 2025 it got 0% on both parts despite asking 1.1-2.7%. For 2026 it asked +5.4% on 340020 and settled +2.4%; it asked +4.0% on 340040 and settled +2.6%. Over the 2026 round it gave up roughly half of its ask. The two zero rounds are the main evidence for this pattern.

Dependency is mixed. On part:340020 it is our single source with 100% quota since 2011, and it owns the tooling, so we depend on it there. On part:340040 it holds 50% alongside sup:70440, which charges about 10.6% more; it won the 2025 benchmark RFQ. On part:340030 it is qualified with 0% quota while sup:70410 holds 100%.

We are a small account to it: about EUR 46k a year, roughly 0.2% of its EUR 22.9M turnover. It is financially sound (equity 38.9%, credit index stable). Its sales director said in May 2026 that they are reviewing small accounts. Our volume pull is weak unless we bundle.

The planned seal kit (about 25,000 kits a year: 2x 340020, 1x 340030, 2x 340040) gives us a bundling lever. Moving 340030 and the remaining 50% of 340040 to this supplier would meaningfully raise our weight with them.

findings.text: Delivery has improved sharply: rolling 12-month OTD rose from 82.4% to 91.8%, the best in nine quarters. It is still below the 95% contract target but well above the peer median of 84.6%. The improvement is uneven by part. Lip seal 340040 was 100% on time on 23 receipts. O-ring set 340020 was 84.6% on time on 26 receipts, with late lines averaging 5.3 days and at most 6 days. Measured over all receipts the lateness was worse (12.6% late, average 13.5 days, maximum 31 days), so the gain is recent.

Quality is mediocre but improving and better than peers. Rolling ppm is 291, down from a 371 peak, against a peer median of 457. There are no overdue 8D reports. Defects nonetheless recur on both parts across many failure modes: leakage at test, wrong material certificates, coating defects and burrs. In the last 12 months there were 7 supplier-caused complaints on 340020 and 5 on 340040, with about EUR 1,500 recharged at the EUR 150 flat fee. These are small sums, but they show that drinking-water and leakage defects persist.

On lip seal 340040 this supplier beats the rival sup:70440 on every measure. Its ppm is 338 against 429. It delivered 100% on time against delays at the rival. Its price is 100.98 per 100 units against the rival's 111.69. Both suppliers hold a 50% quota. The performance record therefore argues for shifting volume to this supplier, not for a price cut.

Our volume outlook is rising, and the forecasts are shared with the supplier. For 340020 we forecast 48,200 pieces over the next 12 months against 44,000 ordered (+9.5%). For 340040 we forecast 39,100 against 37,200 ordered in total, of which 18,740 went to this supplier. A planned kit of about 25,000 a year would need 50,000 of 340020, 25,000 of 340030 and 50,000 of 340040. That is a meaningful lever, given the supplier said it is focusing on customers with volume and our spend is only about 0.2% of its turnover.

There is a price data anomaly to clean up. PO 4500014453-10 for 340020 and PO 4500014319-10 for 340040 were raised at the old prices (63.87 and 98.41) and flagged stale_condition, after the 2026 increases to 65.41 and 100.98. Expect the supplier to raise this. Cite the current prices, not these lines.

Our position on 340020 is weak. This supplier is the sole source with a 100% quota, owns the tooling and has been approved for 15.6 years. Our main counterweight is that its OTD on this part, at 84.6%, is its weakest point.

arguments.text: We are already your cheapest and best-performing source. On the lip seal we sit at 100.98 against Kohlering's 111.69, with lower ppm (338 vs 429) and 100% on-time delivery in the last 12 months. Our benchmark quote of 102.34 beat theirs at 121.27. On the gasket our 1.97 undercut Ravensteiner's 2.35 at 8 days lead time instead of 49. Pushing our price down only widens a gap that already favours you.

Our cost drivers keep rising, and the 2026 settlement did not recover them. Rubber products PPI is up 3.9% in 12 months and stands at its 36-month peak, with roughly 54% weight. Labour cost is up 2.7%, also at its peak, and 10.9% above its 36-month low. Prices on both parts were frozen through 2023 to 2025, so we carried three years of inflation.

We have a history of moderation. We asked 5.4% and 4% last year and settled at 2.4% and 2.6%, and we accepted zero in earlier years. Our owner offered to open our calculation. We are a fair partner, not an opportunist.
Our delivery has improved markedly: OTD is 91.8% in the latest scorecard, the score is 94.5 (class A), and there are no overdue 8Ds. Investment in performance has a cost.
Hollerau's account is small for us, and we are reviewing small accounts. Continued priority needs a sustainable margin or more volume.

weak_points: Our real delivery record on the O-ring set is only 84.6% on time in the last 12 months, and all of our late deliveries were on that part. Both scorecards sit below the 95% contract target.

There is a steady stream of supplier-caused complaints: 20 on the O-ring set, including leakage at test and wrong material certificates, which is sensitive for a drinking-water part. Our ppm is around 300.
The 2026 increase was already granted, and our cost drivers have been modest; power prices are -43% versus 2022.
Our offer to show the calculation could expose our margin.
The 'small account' remark could look like a bluff or a threat. We do want the kit volume, and the customer knows it.
The 90-day notice before year end constrains when we can raise the price.
Kohlering could take the full lip-seal volume if we push too hard.
wants: Award of the full kit: the gasket part:340030 at about 30,600 a year, 100% of the lip seal, and the growing O-ring volume.
A longer contract (24-36 months) with binding annual volume.
Faster payment, for example 14 days, or at least on-time payment, since 84.5% of invoices were paid late.
An index clause on the rubber PPI as an alternative to fixed annual prices.
Correction of the stale-price purchase orders to the current price.
red_lines: No price below the 2026 level on single-source part:340020 without a volume gain.
No higher chargeback per complaint than the current EUR 150, and no ppm commitment we cannot meet.
No multi-year fixed price without either an index clause or binding volume.
We will walk away from small-volume business at a loss rather than subsidise it.
red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for the partnership and point to our improved delivery (94.5 score). Then state that rubber and labour costs are at 36-month peaks and that three frozen years were not fully recovered. Ask for about +4% on both parts for 2027 under the 90-day notice. At the same time, signal openness: if Hollerau bundles the kit with us (gasket at about 2.05-2.10, below its incumbent, plus full lip-seal volume and a 24-month term), we will hold 2027 prices flat or near flat and accept an index clause. Repeat the owner's offer to walk through our calculation.

rebuttals.answer: You are right, and we value it: on the lip seal you are our most competitive and most reliable source, and your gasket benchmark was strong. That is exactly why we want to give you more business rather than squeeze you. We are not asking you to widen any gap through price alone. We want to discuss the whole kit, with the gasket moving to you and a larger lip seal share, at prices that reflect that added volume. Being competitive today is the basis for growth with us, not a reason for an increase.

We accept that rubber and labour costs have risen, and we have checked the indices you name. Weighted by their share of the part cost, they support only a modest change on each part. A large part of that was already covered by the increase we agreed for this year, which took effect from the start of the year. The years of stable prices were agreed renewals during which the drivers were also much flatter, and energy, another cost element, has eased considerably. We are glad to walk through the arithmetic together, and we will gladly take up your owner's offer to go through your calculation on that basis.

We agree, and we appreciate it: your requests have been measured and your settlements fair, and we have always paid reliably in return. That history also shows that both sides have found the right level well below the opening ask, and we would like to continue in that spirit. We accept the owner's offer to go through the calculation together, so that any adjustment rests on shared facts.

The improvement is real and we recognise it. The lip seal in particular has been excellent, and your scorecard has moved up clearly. At the same time, overall delivery is still below the contract target, and the late deliveries sit on the O-ring set. Meeting the agreed target is part of the existing price rather than a reason for an increase. We would rather reward continued performance through more volume and a longer commitment.

We understand that you are focusing on customers with volume, and we would like to be one of them. Our forecasts on the O-ring set and the lip seal are growing, and we plan to source the complete seal kit from one supplier. That would add the gasket and potentially more lip seal volume. We are prepared to commit binding volume and a longer contract in exchange for stable prices. That is a sustainable basis for both sides.

press: We would like to agree a joint improvement plan for the O-ring set, as its delivery performance is still noticeably behind the lip seal and below the agreed target.

Given that the O-ring set is drinking-water approved, we would welcome your corrective actions on the recurring leakage and material certificate complaints, ideally together with a firm ppm commitment.
As this year's increase already reflected much of the recent rubber and labour cost movement, we would like to understand which remaining change you see as justified on a weighted basis.
We would gladly take up your owner's kind offer to walk us through the calculation for both parts.
Under our framework agreement, prices are fixed per calendar year, so we suggest aligning any proposal with the agreed notice process.
We see the kit bundle as the natural way to make our account more valuable to you, and we would like to discuss what pricing it would allow.
